Resolves #18614

Refs #18605

The dock guides now teach the shipped selection idiom instead of stopping at one arrangement and saved records. The panes guide gains a stage-two section: two declared arrangements on the QueueWorkspace, `activePerspective` as the intent, a toolbar inside the workspace whose buttons bind the published name and whose badge binds `modified`, the `activePerspectiveChange` event, the `tab.Container` parallel, and the rule that the workspace publishes into its own provider — the class default or the consumer's — so bindings live there or below, with its reason — ending in a second runnable preview. The two adoption guides state the two name sources plainly (declared perspectives select; saved records are snapshots, with provenance when the capture spreads `perspectiveProvenance()` into its metadata; every write path refuses the engine-reserved `$` names and a library instance wired with `declaredPerspectives` refuses the declared ones on both keys; a document restored alone keeps the committed baseline and a restore descriptor carrying `declaredPerspective` adopts a declared origin; the workspace publishes `active`, `modified` and `pending`, the last never the refresh promise). The zone-model contract's restore rule gains its second sentence. The Neural Link capability matrix's two perspective rows state the shipped tool contract, which the Brain's mirror could not carry because the matrix is an engine document.

`Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029 (as amended)`.

Evidence: L1 (documents; no unit tests for prose) → L3 rendered receipt required by the close target's first criterion (the preview must run and its switcher must work) — achieved on the dev server's portal: the third preview of the panes guide mounts the toolbar and the review arrangement, pressing **Focus** flips the pressed state, moves the queue alone into the center and writes "Selected: focus" into the summary through the change event, with no new console error. Residual: none.

Grounding: the topic is this epic's own graduation and its four merged engine leaves (the author's Memory Core turns of 2026-09-12); every claim in the new prose was exercised against the merged engine before it was written — the preview's classes, verbatim, in the unit runtime (switch, published facts, a committed rearrangement reading Modified, an equal assignment as a no-op, Reset re-applying the baseline: 1 of 1) and the preview itself on the portal.

- The section is placed at the end of the panes guide as a second preview rather than inside the existing journey, so the first preview's narrative (the ownership journey) stays intact and the reader meets selection after ownership.

## Round 1 (Euclid, review 5188476802)
Three claims exceeded the wiring shown. Each was re-derived at the engine, corrected in the text, and pinned by a receipt arm (three arms, 3 of 3 in the unit runtime; a scratch spec beside the preview's, not committed):
- **R1 — publication target.** `PerspectiveState.publishDocument` writes to `workspace.stateProvider`, the own provider, and every dock Workspace declares one by default (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:369`, replaced by the consumer's); `stateProvider: null` removes the target. Measured under a parent seeded with a sentinel: the default child publishes the switch on its own provider and the parent keeps its sentinel; the nulled child resolves the parent's provider for reads, switches, and publishes nothing.
- **R2 — declared-name refusal.** `Persistence.reservedNameErrors(keys, declared)` refuses `$` names unconditionally and declared names only with the list; both instance libraries default `declaredPerspectives` to null and the statics pass no list. Measured: a default `PerspectiveLibrary` saves `focus`; one wired with `() => workspace.declaredPerspectives()` refuses it with the declared-name error; `$mine` is refused without wiring. The guides now show the wiring and the example's explicit `reservedNameErrors(keys, declaredPerspectives())` pass.
- **R3 — provenance and origin.** `createSavedLayout` without metadata stores `{}`; a document-only `onDockZoneDocumentChange` keeps the committed name (`{active: 'focus', modified: true}` after restoring the review snapshot under focus); a descriptor carrying `declaredPerspective` adopts a declared origin (`{active: 'review', modified: false}`) and retains under an undeclared one. The recipe now spreads `perspectiveProvenance()` into the capture and carries the origin on restore, and the example claim states what the merged example does: declared buttons bound, snapshot buttons restoring document-only by design (their captures carry no provenance). Scope, on Euclid's follow-up: the descriptor path is a standalone workspace's — under a Group, `onDockZoneDocumentChange` routes a descriptor without `operation` through `set.write({[workspaceKey]: document})` (`src/dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2423–2425`), which carries no `declaredPerspective`; both guides now name the Group path as the identity entry `perspectiveOriginChange(metadata)` returns riding the Group write, without a snippet, since no shipped consumer writes it yet.

Round 0, outside CI: the rendered receipt on the portal (above), and the preview's classes run verbatim as a scratch spec in the unit runtime — 1 of 1: initial `dock.perspective` `{active: 'review', modified: false, pending: null}` with the Review button pressed; a Focus click through the button's own click path switches the document to the focus baseline, flips the pressed states and writes "Selected: focus"; a committed rearrangement reads `Modified` while an equal assignment stays a no-op; Reset re-applies the baseline. The scratch spec is not committed (a guide's preview is not a tracked test surface); its only deviation from the preview is the ripple effect off, which needs an event path the unit runtime does not supply.
